questions.enonce_markdown:
Examine the role played by Jethro in the life of Moses.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Jethro, priest of Midian, appears at two important moments in the life of Moses: when Moses fled from Egypt and after the Exodus. In the book of Exodus he is also called Reuel (Exodus 2). His role was that of host, father-in-law, employer, counsellor and, possibly, spiritual influence.

**1. Refuge and hospitality.** After killing an Egyptian, Moses fled from Pharaoh to the land of Midian (Exodus 2). At a well he helped the daughters of the priest of Midian, who told their father. Jethro welcomed the fugitive into his household and gave him food and shelter.

**2. Family life.** Jethro gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as wife. Moses settled in Midian and had a son, so Jethro provided him with a family and a new home.

**3. Preparation in the wilderness.** Moses worked as a shepherd for Jethro's flock for many years. It was while tending this flock near Horeb that he met God at the burning bush (Exodus 3). The experience of leading sheep through the desert prepared him to lead Israel there.

**4. Permission to return.** When God told Moses to return to Egypt, Moses asked Jethro for leave to go back to his kinsmen, and Jethro agreed (Exodus 4).

**5. Reunion after the Exodus.** In Exodus 18, Jethro came to the camp of Israel near the mountain of God, bringing Zipporah and the two sons. He rejoiced over everything God had done for Israel, blessed the LORD and said that the LORD was greater than all gods. He offered a sacrifice, and Aaron and the elders ate with him.

**6. Administrative counsel.** Jethro saw that Moses was judging the people alone from morning till evening. He warned that this would wear out both Moses and the people and advised him to teach the people God's laws, to appoint capable and honest men as officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, and to take only the hard cases himself. Moses listened and did as he was advised. This is the origin of a delegated system of justice.

**7. Possible religious influence.** As a priest, Jethro offered sacrifice and shared a meal with Israel's leaders. Some scholars suggest that Moses may have learned something of the worship of Yahweh in Midian, but the text does not say so and this remains a hypothesis.

**Conclusion.** Jethro sheltered Moses, gave him a family, a profession and a period of preparation, and later gave advice that made his leadership effective. He is an example of the wise counsellor who is not an Israelite.
